correctness.rationale: Translate an ordinary k-dominating edge family H of size t in KG(2k+3,2) to d_H(u)+d_H(v)<=t−k for every nonedge uv. At t=k+2, a vertex of degree>=3 would be universal and impossible; degree 2 forces <=3 total edges; degree <=1 is a matching of at most k+1: thus t>=k+3. At equality t=k+3, maximum degree <=3. A degree 3 vertex leads to a K4 or impossible K4−e, forcing k=3 and six K4 edges. Otherwise all degree-2 vertices form a triangle and remaining 2k degree-1 vertices form a perfect matching. Counts are binom(2k+3,3)(2k)!/(2^k k!) plus binom(9,4) at k3. K4 selected edges have only one selected open Kneser neighbor and two closed-neighborhood members, so fail both tuple variants. Independently checked literal domination for K4 and triangle+matching at k3; examined full exhaustive k2,k3 verification source, not claiming to rerun its >2m candidates.
